c.request: Match members to their majors (`member.link_to_major` = `major.major_id`, members with no matching major left out). For each major id and its department, count the members and work out what share of the members that is. Within each department, average the shares of its majors. Show the majors whose share is above their department's average, with the major id, department, member count, share, and how far the share is above the department average. Sort by that difference, largest first (missing values last), and give the top 10. Each major's share uses only members who have a matching major as the denominator.
c.sql: WITH major_counts AS (SELECT ma.major_id, ma.department, COUNT(*) AS member_count FROM member AS me JOIN major AS ma ON me.link_to_major = ma.major_id GROUP BY ma.major_id, ma.department), major_shares AS (SELECT major_id, department, member_count, 1.0 * member_count / SUM(member_count) OVER () AS share FROM major_counts), compared AS (SELECT major_id, department, member_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS difference FROM major_shares) SELECT major_id, department, member_count, share, difference FROM compared WHERE difference > 0 ORDER BY difference IS NULL, difference DESC LIMIT 10;

b.request: For each major with at least one matching member, divide its member count by the total number of members with a matching major; average those shares across majors in each department, then return the 10 majors whose share exceeds their department’s average, showing major ID, department, member count, share, and difference, sorted by difference descending with missing values last.
b.sql: WITH major_counts AS (SELECT major.major_id, major.department, COUNT(*) AS member_count FROM major JOIN member ON member.link_to_major = major.major_id GROUP BY major.major_id, major.department), major_shares AS (SELECT major_id, department, member_count, 1.0 * member_count / SUM(member_count) OVER () AS share FROM major_counts), compared AS (SELECT major_id, department, member_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS difference FROM major_shares) SELECT major_id, department, member_count, share, difference FROM compared WHERE difference > 0 ORDER BY difference DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

a.request: Match each member to their major (`member.link_to_major` = `major.major_id`, members with no matching major left out). For each major id and its department, count the members. Then work out the major's share as that count divided by the total number of members who have a matching major. Within each department, average these shares across its majors. List the majors whose share is above their department's average, showing the major id, department, member count, share, and how far the share is above the department average. Sort by that difference, largest first (missing values last), and return the top 10.
a.sql: WITH major_counts AS (SELECT ma.major_id, ma.department, COUNT(*) AS member_count FROM member AS me JOIN major AS ma ON me.link_to_major = ma.major_id GROUP BY ma.major_id, ma.department), major_shares AS (SELECT major_id, department, member_count, 1.0 * member_count / SUM(member_count) OVER () AS share FROM major_counts), department_shares AS (SELECT major_id, department, member_count, share, AVG(share) OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS department_average FROM major_shares) SELECT major_id, department, member_count, share, share - department_average AS difference FROM department_shares WHERE share > department_average ORDER BY difference IS NULL, difference DESC LIMIT 10;

d.request: Join members to majors on `member.link_to_major = major.major_id`, excluding unmatched members; for each major, divide its member count by the total number of matched members, average those shares across majors within each department, and return the 10 majors whose share exceeds their department’s average, showing major id, department, member count, share, and the difference, sorted by difference descending with missing values last.
d.sql: WITH major_counts AS (SELECT ma.major_id, ma.department, COUNT(*) AS member_count FROM member AS me JOIN major AS ma ON me.link_to_major = ma.major_id GROUP BY ma.major_id, ma.department), major_shares AS (SELECT major_id, department, member_count, 1.0 * member_count / SUM(member_count) OVER () AS share FROM major_counts), compared AS (SELECT major_id, department, member_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS difference FROM major_shares) SELECT major_id, department, member_count, share, difference FROM compared WHERE difference > 0 ORDER BY difference IS NULL, difference DESC LIMIT 10;
